state: Resolve lifecycle policy for AI-authored native Can tests, as documentation only: no builds, live services or measurements. Arbitrary ordinary Can functions own scenarios, expectations, scheduling and reports; eliminate authored host harnesses. The settled architecture uses qualified reference toolchain R to build the judge/controller, fresh Bun case workers, candidate C only as subject, and native supervisor N outside workers. N owns resources, bounds, private transport and recovery; it does not judge expectations. Consumers require Can evidence plus N's cleanup receipt. Existing designs separate subject exit/signal facts from test verdicts, forbid retrying unknown effects, require pre-effect ownership and retain unresolved resource charges. Full qualification needs every retained ledger obligation/environment and full offline roots. Initial bootstrap verifies all roots; a qualified planner may later choose a conservative focused closure. Existing authoring allows exit 0 for a nonempty successfully completed selected subset, exit 1 for completed expectation failures, exit 2 for blocked/incomplete/execution/cleanup failure. Missing selected service is not a pass; unexpected service loss after admission differs from preflight unavailability. Expected subject timeout/crash can pass only if a live reference judge checks the intended facts and cleanup is known; judge death cannot. A failure can coexist with missing later checks and cleanup errors, so preserve these facts rather than overwrite them. User cancellation should stop admission, keep completed evidence, clean externally and leave unstarted selected work visible. Unknown descendant liveness or failed cleanup prevents safe next-case admission; an isolated mismatch or worker fault followed by proven cleanup need not invalidate unrelated evidence. Repeated attempts must not erase earlier failures. Source evidence: current integration harness has three heavy slots by default, per-run content-keyed bundle reuse with hit verification, and separate direct builds for build-subject cases. It rebuilds contaminated entries and removes fill locks by age; those behaviors should not silently conceal contamination or prove safe recovery. Current tempcache has owner/lease/path checks and conservative ps/lsof recovery; failed removal and supervisor death still need durable retained ownership in the new design. Current assertion supervision has deadlines/direct-worker reap but not full descendant/disk enforcement. Proposed initial scheduler remains one active case, one verification worker and one build producer, with finite run-wide resource admission and no speculative build overlap. Cases can require multiple bounded subjects to test concurrency. Existing lifecycle tests have 12-30 minute contexts, so a ten-minute quick profile is not full coverage and cannot automatically omit slow cases. Reuse only immutable verified build results with exact source/dependency/compiler/runtime/options/target identity, inside one owned run, with leases and explicit fresh-build policies for build/determinism/corruption cases. No persistent full bundles/private caches; cleanup must retire staged and ready artifacts, failed fills cannot serve users, and crash recovery is not permission to reuse stale prior-run artifacts.

coverage.instructions: Which report/coverage policy best fits the stated lifecycle requirements?

criteria.separate_axes: Keep selection scope, required-check completion, expectation outcomes, execution integrity and cleanup distinct; allow subset success only when every selected obligation finishes cleanly and reserve full qualification for the whole required matrix.
criteria.single_terminal: Use one terminal case/run status with documented precedence, deriving coverage from those statuses and reducing simultaneous issues to diagnostic annotations.
criteria.environment_optional: Treat unavailable environment legs as automatic skips, allowing a selected run to succeed based on the cases that were executable while reporting the skips separately.

continuation.instructions: What should determine whether later cases can start after a failure?

criteria.containment_gated: Continue independent cases after localized failure only once the owner confirms containment and cleanup; stop admission for cancellation, controller/transport failure, shared artifact corruption or unresolved resources, preserving partial evidence.
criteria.always_fail_fast: Stop scheduling after the first mismatch or execution fault even when containment and cleanup are proved, trading later evidence for the smallest failing run.
criteria.budget_only: Keep dispatching until run limits expire whenever process slots remain, recording cleanup or integrity faults alongside later results instead of making them admission barriers.

reuse.instructions: Which build reuse policy should the lifecycle adopt?

criteria.same_run_verified: Memoize successful identified immutable builds only within the owned run, deduplicate producers, retain read leases, require fresh outputs for build-subject cases, and make unexpected shared corruption a visible error before cleanup rather than an automatic repair.
criteria.fresh_every_case: Build independently for every case and use no shared artifact reuse, simplifying invalidation while increasing repeated staging, compilation and disk activity.
criteria.repair_hits: Retain same-run keyed build reuse but transparently delete and rebuild corrupted or incomplete hits before letting cases proceed, preserving contamination only as cache diagnostics.
